text:
olivia: quick heads-up from running the Go sample app under short deadlines: generator iterator doesn't always fully stop when context is cancelled if auth refresh races. saw a couple leaked goroutines performing refresh retries after Next returned.

nate: can you paste minimal repro + logs?

olivia: repro sketch: use a fake auth provider that sleeps ~900ms, set ctx timeout to 600ms, call iter.Next(ctx) in the usual pull loop. Next returns with deadline, iter.Err() shows context.DeadlineExceeded, but logs keep printing 'auth: refresh start' as background retries continue.

priya: ah yeah, looks like the transport's retry loop or the auth helper is running work detached from the request ctx. two immediate mitigations: (1) add a Close() to the iterator so callers can explicitly signal teardown, (2) make the auth refresh accept a ctx or have the transport select on ctx.Done() during backoff.

nate: adding Close() seems low-risk and helps DX quickly. also update docs so sample app uses defer iter.Close().

olivia: agree. I'll put together a tiny PR for the sample app showing the pattern: iter, _ := client.Generator(ctx, req); defer iter.Close(); for iter.Next(ctx) { ... } and a short note why Close matters for auth edge cases.

priya: test idea: inject a slow auth double in unit tests, cancel after first token, then assert no auth goroutines remain after a small grace window. wrap with eventual consistency to avoid flakes.

nate: also consider ergonomic API: implement io.Closer on iterator, and make Close idempotent and safe to call even if Next already returned. update godoc to recommend defer iter.Close().

olivia: one UX gotcha: new users assume ctx cancel alone is enough. sample app + quickstart should call this out explicitly and link to the FAQ.

priya: long-term audit: we should scan middleware for any goroutines started without a ctx param. Those are the usual suspects. I'll own a follow-up.

ci-bot: created issue #2799 "go: generator iterator should support Close() and make auth refresh cancellation-aware" (assigned to @priya).

olivia: thanks! happy to draft the failing unit test and the sample app patch. I'll include a minimal cancellation-aware retry helper we used locally as a demonstration.

nate: thanks for catching and writing the repro. small changes here will save users a lot of hair-pulling. :raised_hands:
